speaker: Unknown
en: It's time.
zh: 是时候了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can get it started.
zh: 我们可以开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Dan.
zh: 我是 Dan。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm from Maven Clinic.
zh: 我来自 Maven Clinic。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today we will share the experience, how we transition from a traditional technology company to an AI-lative company.
zh: 今天我们将分享经验,我们如何从一家传统科技公司转型为一家 AI 原生公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before I start it, I would like to do a little exercise.
zh: 在开始之前,我想做一个小互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Raise your hand if you think you are already an AI-lative company.
zh: 如果你认为你已经是 AI 原生公司,请举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, we saw a few.
zh: 好,我们看到几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Raise your hand if you thought about it but haven't started the journey yet.
zh: 如果你考虑过但还没有开始这段旅程,请举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, we saw a few.
zh: 好,我们看到几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means most of us is in between.
zh: 这意味着我们大多数人处于两者之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully this talk can help you with that one.
zh: 希望这场演讲能帮到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Maven Clicker is a large digital health platform.
zh: Maven Clicker 是一个大型的数字化健康平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are focused on women and their families.
zh: 我们专注于女性和她们的家庭。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we specialize in like maternity, fertility, parenting, menopause.
zh: 所以我们专注于孕产、生育、育儿、更年期等。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started our AI journey just two years back.
zh: 我们在两年前才开始了我们的 AI 之旅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this moment, we build something called Maven Intelligence.
zh: 在这个时刻,我们构建了一个叫 Maven Intelligence 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's our orchestration nature across all our product to enable AI for everybody in this company and for our clients.
zh: 它是我们跨所有产品的编排层,为公司里的每一个人和我们的客户启用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, AI is here and improving every day.
zh: 所以,AI 已经在这里,并且每天都在进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think adopting it is not optional.
zh: 我认为采用它不是可选的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if you choose not to, your competitors will do.
zh: 即使你选择不采用,你的竞争对手也会采用。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a code I heard like a couple years back.
zh: 这是我几年前听到的一个说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would like to share here again.
zh: 我想在这里再分享一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like tranctures want to replace farmers, but the farmers who can operate the tranctor will replace the ones who cannot.
zh: 就像拖拉机想要取代农民,但会操作拖拉机的农民将取代不会操作的农民。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully everybody here will become farmers who can operate your tranctures.
zh: 希望在座的每个人都会成为能操作你们拖拉机的农民。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the goal.
zh: 这就是目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first of all, I don't think there's one single definition what it means by AI native.
zh: 首先,我不认为对 AI 原生意味着什么有一个单一的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more importantly, there's no predefined playbook.
zh: 更重要的是,没有预先定义好的操作手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can just follow and bingo, you become AI native.
zh: 你可以直接照着做,然后叮,你就变成 AI 原生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, it has really come down to three parts.
zh: 对我们来说,它真正归结为三个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is internally without AI tools whenever it's possible.
zh: 一是在内部,只要有可能就使用 AI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be as simple as generating your daily summary, managing your meeting, create a Jira task.
zh: 它可以简单到生成你的每日摘要、管理你的会议、创建一个 Jira 任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you need to do today manually, you should think about to say, can you use AI to do it?
zh: 今天任何你需要手动做的事情,你都应该想一想,能不能用 AI 来做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever you want to ask other people to do something for you,
zh: 每当你想让别人为你做某件事时,

speaker: Unknown
en: You should say, I can use AI to do it.
zh: 你应该说,我可以用 AI 来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of leaders, in fact, today at Maven, include our CIOs, they use AI2 to solve those tasks by themselves now, instead to delegate to other people.
zh: 很多领导者,实际上,今天在 Maven,包括我们的 CIO 们,他们现在都自己用 AI2 来解决那些任务,而不是委派给别人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's for internally.
zh: 那是内部的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Externally, we want to build AIs into our product.
zh: 在外部,我们想把 AI 构建进我们的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We achieve two goals there.
zh: 我们在那里实现了两个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is really focused on input our user experience.
zh: 一是真正专注于改善我们的用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second, maybe help us reduce our operational cost.
zh: 第二,也许能帮我们降低运营成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like AI-based, like Chatbot is a really good example.
zh: 比如 AI 聊天机器人就是一个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 24-7, always available, can help address issues, help our customer instantly.
zh: 它 24-7 全天候可用,可以帮助解决问题,即时帮助我们的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's way better and cheaper compared to human agents.
zh: 相比人工代理,它好得多也更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thirdly, and I think it's more important, we need to think about culture, process, the way we work, how we can change it so we can maximize what the AI offers for us.
zh: 第三,我认为这更重要,我们需要思考文化、流程、我们的工作方式,我们如何改变它们,以便最大化 AI 为我们提供的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will touch it more on the following slides.
zh: 我会在接下来的幻灯片中更多地谈到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we come to adopting new technologies, there's always three groups of users.
zh: 当我们采用新技术时,总是有三类用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, there's some early adopters.
zh: 一,有一些早期采用者。

speaker: Unknown
en: For them, we don't need to do too much.
zh: 对他们,我们不需要做太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Only thing we need to do is enable the tools for them and encourage them to share what they learn with the company.
zh: 我们唯一需要做的就是为他们启用工具,并鼓励他们把学到的分享给公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we need to really focus on is the one in the middle.
zh: 而我们真正需要关注的是中间的那一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the majority.
zh: 那是大多数人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should build a shared infrastructure for them, build easy-to-use tools for them, just make the adoption as seamlessly as possible.
zh: 我们应该为他们构建共享基础设施，为他们构建易用的工具，只是让采用尽可能无缝。

speaker: Unknown
en: More importantly, we should really listen to them, get feedback, consistently improving.
zh: 更重要的是，我们应该真正倾听他们，获取反馈，持续改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, last year, most of folks at Maven, they are using Cursor.
zh: 举个例子，去年 Maven 的大部分人都在用 Cursor。

speaker: Unknown
en: This year, a lot of them switched to cloud codes.
zh: 今年，他们中很多人切换到了 cloud codes。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, we need to support both.
zh: 对我们来说，我们需要同时支持两者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to meet where they are, just to make sure they're comfortable to use it.
zh: 我们需要在他们所在之处与之相会，只是确保他们用起来是舒适的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all the places, you always have a few slow adopters.
zh: 而且在任何地方，总会有少数慢的采用者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They always have concerns, worries for the new technologies.
zh: 他们对新技术总是有顾虑、有担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: For them, we just should meet where they are.
zh: 对他们，我们就应该在他们所在之处与之相会。

speaker: Unknown
en: understand what their concern is.
zh: 理解他们的顾虑是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But more important, we should be crystal clear with them where the company is heading to.
zh: 但更重要的是，我们应该对他们非常清楚地说明公司正走向何方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So AI is really good at execution if we know what we want to do.
zh: 所以 AI 真的很擅长执行，只要我们知道我们想做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's change how we should hire new people and how should we reward it.
zh: 所以让我们改变招聘新人的方式，以及我们应该如何给予奖励。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to, the way we used to work is we have a senior engineer who sense the problem, come up with a solution and dedicate to other engineers
zh: 我们过去的工作方式是：我们有一位资深工程师感知问题，想出解决方案，然后分派给其他工程师

speaker: Unknown
en: for implementation so we can work in parallel and be faster.
zh: 去做实现，这样我们就可以并行工作、更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these days, we found that NASA engineers would like to dedicate implementation work to other people because they already figured out how to solve the problem.
zh: 但这些天，我们发现 NASA 工程师不愿意把实现工作分派给其他人，因为他们已经想清楚了怎么解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just use AI to solve it instantly.
zh: 他们只是用 AI 立刻把它解决掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dedicating to other people means more overheads and way less efficient.
zh: 分派给其他人意味着更多开销，效率低得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also means when you have new people, you want to make sure they can solve the problem independently.
zh: 这也意味着，当你有新人时，你要确保他们能独立解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: They pretty much have to work on the traditional technical level.
zh: 他们几乎必须在传统的技术层面上工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We cannot afford other people to dedicate an implementation task for them.
zh: 我们无法承担让别人为他们分派实现任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, when we hire new people, we should think about what we are looking for.
zh: 另外，当我们招新人时，我们应该思考我们在寻找什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We definitely want to look for somebody genuinely interested in AI.
zh: 我们肯定想找真正对 AI 感兴趣的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The domain is moving so fast.
zh: 这个领域变化非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want them to keep learning, also help the team to stay on track.
zh: 我们希望他们持续学习，也帮助团队保持正轨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Secondly is
zh: 其次是

speaker: Unknown
en: With AI, engineers can do way more than they used to do.
zh: 有了 AI,工程师能做的远比以前多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The boundaries between PM and engineers is getting blurry.
zh: PM 和工程师之间的边界正在变得模糊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We found engineers who really understand the product, in fact, they can have way more contribution than the traditional engineer who only focus on software side.
zh: 我们发现真正理解产品的工程师，事实上，他们的贡献可以远大于只专注于软件侧的传统工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is what we are looking for.
zh: 而这正是我们在寻找的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those deep understanding of the system
zh: 还有那些对系统的深刻理解

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to handle complicated, ambiguous problem is also very valuable.
zh: 处理复杂、模糊问题的能力也非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where AI rank off.
zh: 这正是 AI rank off 的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we hire new people, this is also the people we are interested in bringing on boards.
zh: 当我们招新人时，这也是我们感兴趣引入的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: For people we bring in, we want to reward them in the proper way.
zh: 对于我们引入的人，我们想以恰当的方式奖励他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even in our performance review, we start to ask, okay, what you have done for AI side?
zh: 甚至在我们的绩效评估中，我们开始问：好，你在 AI 方面做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We definitely want to reward the people who leverage AI to multiple,
zh: 我们肯定想奖励那些利用 AI 来倍增

speaker: Unknown
en: their impact, although this is the impact for everybody in the company.
zh: 他们影响力的人，尽管这是对全公司每个人都有影响的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have the right tools, we get the right talent in the place, and we need to change how we work to maximize the benefit of AI.
zh: 所以现在我们有了合适的工具，把合适的人才放到了位置上，我们还需要改变我们的工作方式，以最大化 AI 的收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way we used to work is to say, okay, we spend the weeks, sometimes it's the months, to flesh out the business requirements, finalize the design, adding
zh: 我们过去的工作方式是说：好，我们花几周，有时是几个月，来充实业务需求、敲定设计、添加

speaker: Unknown
en: Do the implementation.
zh: 做实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because implementation can be really expensive.
zh: 因为实现可能非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we didn't get the other part right at the beginning, it can be very costly to change it later.
zh: 如果我们一开始没有把另外的部分做对，之后再去改的代价会非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in fact, we never get the same thing right at the beginning anyway for any of our big projects.
zh: 但事实上，对于任何一个大项目，我们从来就没有在一开始就把它做对过。

speaker: Unknown
en: With AI, building is super fast.
zh: 有了 AI,构建非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably a couple minutes.
zh: 可能只需要几分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can get it done.
zh: 你就能把它做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: Argument is really expensive one.
zh: Argument 是真正昂贵的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we should really think about what's the best way we can work, how can we deliver fast.
zh: 所以我们真的应该思考什么是最好的工作方式，我们如何能快速交付。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still OK. You can think about what you want to deliver in one year.
zh: 现在还是可以的。你可以想想一年内想交付什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can assume AI models can do anything you want in one year.
zh: 你可以假设一年内 AI 模型能做任何你想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Based on that one, really dream big to think what you can do in one year.
zh: 基于这一点，大胆地去梦想一年内你能做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it should only serve as inspiring and directional.
zh: 但它只能作为激励和方向性的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we really need to focus on is what we want to deliver in the next two to four weeks.
zh: 我们真正需要聚焦的是未来两到四周内我们想交付什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we want to get the PMs and designers to say, OK, tell me what I need to do in this sprint.
zh: 我们想让 PM 和设计师说：好，告诉我这个迭代周期里我需要做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the engineer will focus on it and get it released at the end of the sprint if not sooner.
zh: 工程师专注于此，并在迭代周期结束时（如果不是更早）把它发布出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, the PMs, they have time to flesh out the next bunch of the requirements.
zh: 与此同时，PM 有时间去充实下一批需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: If under this sprint, they say, no, what we decided 2xGo is wrong, it's totally OK. We can switch the gear, get it fixed quickly.
zh: 如果在这个迭代周期内，他们说：不，我们之前决定的方向是错的，那完全没问题。我们可以换挡，快速修正。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also means we prefer people not to write pages or pages of PRD or TDD anymore.
zh: 这也意味着我们更希望大家不再写一页又一页的 PRD 或 TDD。

speaker: Unknown
en: We prefer them to write just a short one or two pages.
zh: 我们更希望他们只写一到两页的简短文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: That one really serves as communication, so we can iterate on it.
zh: 那份文档真正起到的是沟通作用，这样我们可以在其上迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: The really awkward part is the midterm goals.
zh: 真正尴尬的部分是中期目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are like three months, six months.
zh: 那些大概是三个月、六个月的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to plan these days.
zh: 如今规划这些非常困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason is I don't know what AI models will be capable in three months.
zh: 原因是我不知道三个月内 AI 模型会有什么能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There may be multiple releases already.
zh: 到那时可能已经发布了多个版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we prefer not to focus on this one.
zh: 所以我们倾向于不聚焦这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this one can maybe make it very easy for most of the folks who has been in this domain for a long time because traditionally we get used to have quarterly planning or we plan it for six months.
zh: 但这一点对在这个领域待了很久的大多数人来说可能很难适应，因为传统上我们习惯做季度规划，或者规划六个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's our job to get used to the new AI era and learn how to work it efficiently.
zh: 但适应新的 AI 时代、学会如何高效地工作，是我们的职责。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I want to talk about coding and software development a little bit more here.
zh: 所以我想在这里多聊聊编程和软件开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI coding tools is probably the most successful AI application.
zh: AI 编程工具可能是最成功的 AI 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really good in implementation.
zh: 它在实现方面真的很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably heard a lot of people say, OK, I have this AI tools.
zh: 你可能听很多人说过：好，我有这些 AI 工具了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I can even use my phone to implement software and automate every staging.
zh: 现在我甚至可以用手机来实现软件并自动化每个环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they feel comfortable to do that, it's totally OK.
zh: 如果他们觉得这样做很自在，那完全没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you don't have to.
zh: 但你不必如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm trying to say here is
zh: 我在这里想说的是——

speaker: Unknown
en: And Maven, this is our journey, how we adopt those AI tools.
zh: 还有 Maven，这是我们的历程，我们是如何采用那些 AI 工具的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started with the lowest risk task, like starting with writing unit hands documentation.
zh: 我们从风险最低的任务开始，比如先从写单元测试和文档开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things are very easy to verify, and the risk is super low.
zh: 那些东西非常容易验证，风险也极低。

speaker: Unknown
en: By doing that one, we build the confidence.
zh: 通过做这些，我们建立了信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we start to construct our own rules, skills, and build our guardrails.
zh: 然后我们开始构建自己的规则、技能，并建立我们的护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we push to the whole engineer team, say, now you should use this AI coding tools for all the tasks.
zh: 接着我们推广到整个工程师团队，说：现在你们应该在所有任务上都使用这些 AI 编程工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: When they choose not to, it's the time we really want to learn, say, why you don't do it?
zh: 当他们选择不用时，正是我们真正想了解的时候：你为什么不用？

speaker: Unknown
en: And at this moment, we pretty much use the AI coding tools to do all our implementation.
zh: 而此刻，我们几乎用 AI 编程工具来完成所有的实现工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineers really focus on reviewing, architecturing, and evaluation.
zh: 工程师真正专注于审查、架构设计和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, and with AI coding tools, we are writing so much code these days.
zh: 所以，有了 AI 编程工具，我们如今写了非常多的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Code review becomes really challenging.
zh: 代码审查变得非常有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for a good engineer, used to, they probably write hundreds or less code every day.
zh: 以前，一个好工程师大概每天写几百行以内的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: These days, they can easily write like thousands.
zh: 如今，他们轻松就能写上千行。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we're capable to do the code review as we used to do, we won't be able to keep up.
zh: 如果我们还想像以前那样做代码审查，我们将跟不上节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also tried multiple AI coding review tools.
zh: 我们也尝试了多款 AI 代码审查工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It helps a little bit, but we don't feel comfortable 100% rely on them yet.
zh: 有一点帮助，但我们还不能 100% 放心地依赖它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still found the feedback from our engineers are very, very valuable.
zh: 我们仍然发现来自我们工程师的反馈非常非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means we need to really change the way we are doing code review to meet where we are now.
zh: 这意味着我们必须真正改变做代码审查的方式，以适应当下的现状。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a couple of things we have done.
zh: 我们做了几件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is we allow engineers to self-identify whether we still need code review.
zh: 一是允许工程师自行判断是否还需要代码审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they think this PR is simple enough, I feel very confident, I don't need anybody to take a look.
zh: 如果他们认为这个 PR 足够简单，我非常有信心，不需要任何人来看一眼。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are fine with that one.
zh: 我们对那一点没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We leave them merge, but we still hold them accountable.
zh: 我们允许他们合并，但我们仍然让他们承担责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they do want code review, we want them to stay with the best practices.
zh: 如果他们确实想要代码审查，我们希望他们保持最佳实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, each PR shouldn't have more than 500 lines of code because nobody can
zh: 例如，每个 PR 不应该超过 500 行代码，因为没有人能

speaker: Unknown
en: Do a meaningful code review with the ones that has like thousands of less code.
zh: 对那些有几千行代码的东西做出有意义的代码审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also enabled like stanked PR.
zh: 我们还启用了像 stanked PR 这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it means is that for big feature and the engineers can break it into multiple PRs while people review the PRs and they can keep working on it.
zh: 它的意思是，对于大的功能，工程师可以把它拆成多个 PR,当人们在审查这些 PR 的时候，他们可以继续在上面工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing we really want to avoid is a rubber stamp, we call it.
zh: 我们真正想避免的一件事就是我们所说的“橡皮图章”。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means people submit code review.
zh: 它是指人们提交代码审查。

speaker: Unknown
en: You cannot really do anything to it.
zh: 你实际上什么也做不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just say, blindly prove it.
zh: 你只是盲目的说，批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the worst case we should really avoid, because that just gives us false confidence.
zh: 这是我们真正应该避免的最坏情况，因为那只会给我们虚假的信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think we reviewed it, it's good, and we release it.
zh: 我们以为我们审查过了，它是好的，然后我们就发布它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, we should keep working on our AI code review tools, because we think that's the future.
zh: 同时，我们应该继续开发我们的 AI 代码审查工具，因为我们认为那是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at this moment, we use AI tools pretty much assisting on each step of our software development.
zh: 所以在此时此刻，我们在软件开发的每一步都在大量使用 AI 工具来辅助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our goal is it will be automating the whole lifecycle from end to end, from designing, implementation, until it's fully released.
zh: 我们的目标是它将自动化整个生命周期，从端到端，从设计、实现，直到完全发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: More importantly, we want the AI tools to be able to monitor the live traffic and be able to catch the issue early and automatically fix it.
zh: 更重要的是，我们希望 AI 工具能够监控线上流量，能够及早发现问题并自动修复。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what we are still working on and we are not there yet.
zh: 这就是我们仍在努力的方向，我们还没到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last thing I want to touch a little bit for this presentation is about reliability.
zh: 在这次演讲中我想稍微谈到的最后一件事是关于可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what it means is like for the traditional software, it does what we implement there.
zh: 它的意思是，对于传统软件，它只做我们在那里实现的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: No more, no less.
zh: 不多，不少。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for the GNI solutions, hallucination is there.
zh: 但对于 GNI 解决方案，幻觉是存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We cannot ignore it.
zh: 我们不能忽视它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Completely eliminating them can be very costly.
zh: 完全消除它们可能非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes it's not necessary either.
zh: 有时候也没有必要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way we should do is really have a holistic solution, even from the beginning.
zh: 所以我们应该做的是从一开始就有一个整体的解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, we can start with identifying which failures are exemptable, which ones are not exemptable.
zh: 例如，我们可以先识别哪些失败是可豁免的，哪些不是可豁免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: For our AI system, for example, we have the functionality to help our customers to schedule appointments.
zh: 对于我们的 AI 系统，例如，我们有帮助客户预约日程的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we fail one out of one thousand, probably it's okay.
zh: 如果一千次中我们失败一次，大概没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not saying it's a good experience, but the users usually can just click the button again, we will reschedule for them.
zh: 我不是说那是好的体验，但用户通常只需再点一次按钮，我们会为他们重新安排。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably it's okay.
zh: 大概没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we help a user to submit their reimbursement claim,
zh: 但如果我们帮一个用户提交他们的报销申请，

speaker: Unknown
en: We cannot tolerate a failure, because if people ask of $200, we issue them $50, or they ask $50, we give them $200.
zh: 我们不能容忍失败，因为如果人们申请 200 美元，我们给他们发了 50 美元，或者他们申请 50 美元，我们给了他们 200 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each case will cause an escalation right away.
zh: 每个这种情况都会立刻引发一次升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: For those cases, we have to put in extra stamps.
zh: 对于那些情况，我们必须加入额外的关卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, when we receive their receipt, we will use different models to review the same receipt.
zh: 例如，当我们收到他们的收据时，我们会用不同的模型来审查同一张收据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We only move forward if the results from different models agree with each other.
zh: 只有当不同模型的结果彼此一致时，我们才继续往下走。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we really have trouble to figure it out, which one is right?
zh: 如果我们真的很难弄清楚，哪个是对的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy.
zh: 很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's okay to tell the customer, say, hey, I have trouble to process your stuff.
zh: 告诉客户是可以的，说，嘿，我处理你的东西遇到了困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you want us to get you connect to a human agent?
zh: 你想让我们帮你转接到一个人工智能体吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We will move from there.
zh: 我们会从那里继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's our sample solutions.
zh: 那是我们的示例解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, we should have a rigorous process to release our software.
zh: 另外，我们应该有一个严格的流程来发布我们的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, we have like hundreds of integration tests, which pretty much covered all the use cases we know, and we keep adding to the integration test suite.
zh: 对我们来说，我们有几百个集成测试，几乎覆盖了我们已知的所有用例，并且我们持续向集成测试套件中添加。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we run the integration test,
zh: 当我们运行集成测试时，

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only pass once is not good enough anymore because the ARM can do different things.
zh: 只通过一次已经不够好了，因为 ARM 可以做出不同的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for each test case we run it many times.
zh: 所以对每个测试用例，我们运行很多次。

speaker: Unknown
en: We consistently requires a high pass rate, like for example 90% for all the time.
zh: 我们持续要求高通过率，比如例如始终保持 90%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more important, after we launched the software, we have our auto-evolve system, carefully evaluated each conversation.
zh: 更重要的是，在我们上线软件之后，我们有我们的自动演化系统，仔细评估每一次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have predefined a lot of rubrics, what we think is good, what is bad.
zh: 我们预先定义了很多评分标准，哪些是我们认为好的，哪些是坏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we will general results.
zh: 然后我们会得到一般性的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will review the score.
zh: 我们会审查这些分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Besides this one, we also have a dedicated group.
zh: 除此之外，我们还有一个专门的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their job is manually review those conversations.
zh: 他们的工作是人工审查那些对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will spot check our conversations.
zh: 我们会对我们的对话进行抽查。

speaker: Unknown
en: That helps us to say whether we need to come back to improve our systems, or our rubrics is too strict or too loose, and we need to consistently improve it.
zh: 这能帮助我们判断是否需要回头改进我们的系统，或者我们的评分标准是太严还是太松，并且我们需要持续不断地改进它。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we launch new features, that's the time we say spot check probably not enough.
zh: 当我们发布新功能时，那时候我们会说，抽查可能不够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really want to review, say, 20%, and we can do it.
zh: 我们真的想审查，比如说，20%，而且我们能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: This whole process makes sure we feel really confident we never reach something, although we know hallucination is there.
zh: 这整个过程确保我们非常有信心永远不会碰到某些东西，尽管我们知道幻觉是存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty much all I have for today, and I can stay here to take up questions, and if you have other things, you can reach out to me.
zh: 这基本就是我今天要讲的全部内容了，我可以留在这里回答问题，如果你们有其他事情，也可以联系我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
